summary: I re-downloaded every primary source and re-derived every number myself; I confirm the metric records for SPRC (54.92/74.97/64.85), CSMCIR (57.07/77.27/67.17), CLIP4Cir RN50x4 fullft (43.78/66.93, mean correctly null with 55.36 marked WORKBENCH_DERIVED), HINT (58.48/77.93), ENCODER (56.13/77.59) and PAIR (52.76/74.51), all from sha256-identical PDFs where the PDF was reachable (SPRC 2c250ddb..., CLIP4Cir 497c5921..., HINT fbe97798..., CSMCIR camera-ready e449ceb2... and arXiv v3 878907fc...) plus author-rendered images and the CSMCIR author training log (epoch 9: 57.0670/77.2672/67.1671), and I separately verified the CSMCIR FashionIQ checkpoint digest c8812071... at HF revision cf0c19bb... and the HINT/PAIR file listings. Three premises I was asked to test are REFUTED BY EVIDENCE rather than confirmed: (1) the SPRC table is NOT Shirt|Dress|Toptee - the camera-ready body header is Dress|Shirt|Toptee and four independent renderings agree, so the record's per-category mapping is right; (2) the CLIP4Cir paper really has NO Combiner-only RN50x4 FashionIQ row - 'noft' appears 0 times, 'out-of-the-box' appears only in prose and figure captions, Tables 1-8 are RN-50-only and the two RN50x4 rows are both fully fine-tuned - so the workbench's nulls for combiner_rn50x4_noft are correct for the cited paper (the artefact exists as fiq_comb_RN50x4_noft.pt with no result row, and the vocabulary split the assignment predicted is real: paper says 'out-of-the-box', the release folders say 'noft'/'fullft', the pinned repo's README mentions neither); (3) the registry really does null sprc reported_r10, and the record's asserted consequence is too strong - the runtime paper_gate DOES compare 54.92 (I ran it: reproduced r10 of 0.0 and 5.0 fail, 54.92 passes), while the disabled check is the separate metrics_extraction._check_parity/autopilot path. What a reader must not trust: (a) the extracted csmcir experiment has no paper_id of its own and the offline builder stamped paper_id 'sprc' onto the committed CSMCIR reference (papers.yaml:1821), so any consumer resolving a reference's paper by paper_id gets the SPRC paper for CSMCIR; (b) every paper's own Average column is internally inconsistent with the per-category cells it prints, and by different amounts - SPRC Average R@10 is +0.197 pp above the macro of its own Dress/Shirt/Toptee cells while its Avg. 64.85 equals the mean of the recomputed macros, CSMCIR is -0.027 pp on Average R@10 and +0.087 pp on Average R@50 (systematic, repeated in its Tables 5 and 6), CLIP4Cir/HINT/PAIR are within 0.003 pp - and the record's account is thinner and partly misdirected on SPRC (its +0.197 explanation is width-weighting, which my width-weighted recomputation does not reproduce: 54.919, still short of 54.92); (c) the CSMCIR paper's dress R@50 of 74.81 is not reproduced by the published epoch-9 log (75.0620), so state that cell as not-resumed rather than verified; (d) the pair record's prose transposes the CVPR22 demo paper's Dress and Shirt pairs, and its numbers (like ENCODER's) rest on author-rendered figures because the IEEE and AAAI PDFs were not readable from this host. Nothing here turns an UNKNOWN into a PASS, and nothing in this assignment was RUNTIME_VERIFIED - no GPU inference was possible and no checkpoint bytes were loaded; every numeric conclusion is STATIC_AUDIT against a downloaded artefact, with the one executable fact being the in-process gate/parity behaviour of the committed Python.
